# :open_book: The Book of AI - Mapping the practical Artificial Intelligence landscape
:toolbox: _The Book of Agentic AI — A practical guide to understanding agents and building a practical toolkit._

The Book of AI is an attempt to be a practical guide to understanding agents and building an AI toolkit you control. It is a living document, and the landscape is changing rapidly. The book is structured to provide both a high-level overview and practical guidance for building and using agentic AI systems.

This book focuses on [{{< glossary "Agentic Engineer" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#agentic-engineer) — the disciplined practice of designing, orchestrating, and governing systems of AI agents that plan, act, observe, and iterate — and on the [{{< glossary "Agentic engineering stack" popup="hover" >}}](https://davidgeeraerts.github.io/AI/appendices/glossary.html#agentic-engineering-stack): the layered set of models, harnesses, tools, memory, orchestration, and governance required to make those agents reliable and controllable in real work.

Use this book as a living toolkit: consult the chapters for practical
orientation, and follow the linked source materials and quarterly snapshots as
the landscape changes.


## The Shift to Agentic Engineering
As artificial intelligence moves beyond single-turn conversational models, the focus of development has shifted toward agentic engineering—the discipline of designing, orchestrating, and deploying autonomous AI systems capable of complex reasoning, tool use, and multi-step execution.

To build and scale these systems, developers rely on the agentic engineering stack. This stack transitions AI from monolithic applications into a modular, highly configurable ecosystem, typically comprising:

The Reasoning Engine: The foundational models that interpret intent and drive logic.

Orchestration & Frameworks: The control layer for planning, multi-agent delegation, and context efficiency (utilizing paradigms found in tools like Agent Zero, SpyNEL, or AGENTS.md).

Tooling & Execution Environments: Sandboxed, terminal-first execution layers (such as Podman containers) that allow agents to safely run scripts, manipulate files, and interface with external APIs.

Memory & State Management: The infrastructure for maintaining both short-term working context and long-term persistent data retrieval.

Mastering this stack is essential for moving from isolated prompts to robust, self-directed workflows that integrate seamlessly with local hardware and custom system administration tools.
